<|START_TEXT|>Australia does not observe GMT; it uses multiple time zones.
Australia's time zones are UTC+8, UTC+9:30, UTC+10, and UTC+11.
Australia's time zones are ahead of GMT by 8, 9.5, 10, or 11 hours depending on location.
UTC+8 is Western Standard Time (Western Australia).
UTC+9:30 is Central Standard Time (South Australia and Northern Territory).
UTC+10 is Eastern Standard Time (Queensland, New South Wales, Victoria, Tasmania, ACT).
UTC+11 is used during daylight saving in New South Wales, Victoria, Tasmania, and the ACT.
Queensland does not observe daylight saving and remains on UTC+10 year-round.
Western Australia does not observe daylight saving and remains on UTC+8 year-round.
South Australia does not observe daylight saving and remains on UTC+9:30 year-round.
New South Wales, Victoria, Tasmania, and the ACT switch between UTC+10 and UTC+11 for daylight saving.<|END_TEXT|>

Arabic is the official language of 22 countries in the Arab League.
It is spoken in Algeria, Bahrain, Comoros, Djibouti, Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Mauritania, Morocco, Oman, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, Sudan, Syria, Tunisia, United Arab Emirates, and Yemen.
It is also widely spoken in Chad, Eritrea, Israel, Mali, Niger, and Senegal.
Arabic is used in religious contexts by Muslims worldwide.
It is a liturgical language for Islam.
It is used in diaspora communities in Europe, the Americas, and Australia.

Muslims accept the Prophet Muhammad as the final messenger and the Quran as the ultimate revelation.  
The faith includes belief in angels, previous prophets, the Day of Judgment, and divine destiny.  
The Five Pillars—declaration of faith, prayer, fasting, almsgiving, and pilgrimage—form the foundation of practice.  
Islamic teachings stress moral responsibility, justice, compassion, and submission to God's will.<|END_TEXT|>
